item.title: Estimates for a Parameterized Hankel Functional of Starlike Mappings of Order $\alpha$ and Quasi-Convex Mappings of Type $B$ in Complex Banach Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.33031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce and investigate a parameterized Hankel-type functional $$H_{2,2}^{\mu}(f)=\mu a_2a_4-a_3^2,\qquad \mu\in[0,1], $$ which reduces to the classical second-order Hankel determinant $H_{2,2}(f)$ when $\mu=1$. We obtain estimates for $H_{2,2}^{\mu}(f)$ over the class of starlike mappings of order $\alpha$ on the unit ball of a complex Banach space and on the unit polydisk $\mathbb{U}^n$ in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We also establish estimates for $H_{2,2}^{\mu}(f)$ over the class of quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ on the unit ball of a complex Banach space and on the unit polydisk $\mathbb{U}^n$. For $\mu=1$, our results recover the corresponding estimates for the classical Hankel determinant and extend the known one-dimensional results of Cho et al. \cite{Cho-2018} and Thomas et al. \cite{Thomas-Tuneski} to higher-dimensional settings.
item.dc:creator: Sujoy Majumder, Abhijit Banerjee, Shantanu Panja, Debabrata Pramanik

item.title: Three BMO-type Spaces Characterizing Chord--Arc Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.33067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we introduce three BMO-type spaces on a locally rectifiable Jordan curve and prove that it is a chord-arc curve if and only if these spaces coincide with equivalent norms.
item.dc:creator: Liu Tailiang, Shen Yuliang

item.title: Radial reduction, spherical splitting and root counts for two-sided quaternionic polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.33082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quaternionic polynomials whose coefficients may occur on both sides of the variable, using their degree in the four real coordinates. Such polynomials can have no roots, or many more isolated roots than their degree. A simple root has an invertible real derivative, and its sign is the sign of that derivative's determinant. For a radial family, the roots over a non-real target reduce to one real equation. We obtain a sharp root bound and follow a change in the signed root count as roots escape to infinity. The main results concern spherical root sets for which the polynomial derivative is invertible in the two normal directions. Under a small polynomial perturbation, a sphere splits into simple roots corresponding to the zeros of a tangent vector field, when the derivative of that field is invertible at every zero. We obtain a sharp bound in terms of the perturbation degree and a signed count of two or of minus two. For even degrees, the construction yields polynomials with a single leading power and lower-degree terms whose simple root counts, divided by the fourth power of the degree, tend to one as the degree grows. An explicit quartic has 132 simple roots, and this count persists under small coefficient perturbations. For gradient perturbations, the roots correspond to equilibrium directions of an energy on the sphere. This correspondence gives energy thresholds for root disappearance and bounds the critical directions of polynomial orientation profiles in diffusion magnetic resonance imaging.
item.dc:creator: R. Laniewski

item.title: Berezin Transform Commutators
item.description: arXiv:2610.33937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study commutators of Berezin transforms $\mathcal B_\alpha$ associated with radial weighted Fock spaces with exponential weights $e^{-\alpha |z|^{m}}$ on the complex plane. We prove that when $m>2$, the commutator $[\mathcal B_\alpha,\mathcal B_\beta]$ is compact on the space $L^{2}(\mathbb C, dA)$ whenever $\alpha,\beta>0$. We further show that if $m>2$ and $\alpha\neq\beta$, then the commutator is never of finite rank.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Borichev, G\'erard Fantolini, El-Hassan Youssfi

item.title: Integrable distortion II: the p-Weil-Petersson variational problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.34007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the hyperbolically weighted distortion energies \[ \mathcal{I}_p(f)=\int_\mathbb{D} \frac{|\mu_f|^p}{(1-|\mu_f|^2)^{\max\{2,p\}/2}}\,dA_\eta \] for finite-distortion disk homeomorphisms with prescribed boundary values, together with the associated inverse problem in the monotone Sobolev class. For $1<p\leq2$, the inverse density is polyconvex precisely when $p\geq p_{\mathrm c}=1+1/\sqrt2$. In this range, quasisymmetric data with finite-energy monotone barriers yield minimisers with holomorphic Ahlfors--Hopf differentials and strong local Sobolev convergence of minimising subsequences. For $p_{\mathrm c}<p<2$, a finite-energy finite-distortion barrier yields a unique absolute monotone minimiser, which is a quasiconformal diffeomorphism and is asymptotically conformal. Together with the boundary-class theorem of Part~I, this characterises the admissible boundary data as $T^p$. The proof combines a selected barrier approximation, uniform scalar gradient estimates and a weighted Reich--Strebel comparison. For $1<p<p_{\mathrm c}$, finite rank-one comparisons bound distortion on the positive-Jacobian set by a cutoff strictly below the ellipticity cutoff. An attained monotone minimum is either a quasiconformal diffeomorphism or has nonzero rank-one derivatives on a set of positive area. For $0<p\leq1$, minimisers with finite distortion, or homeomorphic minimisers with a locally Sobolev inverse, are M\"obius maps. We also obtain energy-dependent quasiconformal bounds for regular minimisers when $p>2$. \
item.dc:creator: Gaven Martin, Cong Yao

item.title: Hyperbolic complex tangencies on a four-sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.34219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a smooth embedding of $S^4$ into $\mathbb C^4$ whose CR-singular locus is a connected surface of genus two consisting entirely of nondegenerate hyperbolic points. Its image is locally polynomially convex and admits a basis of smoothly bounded, strongly pseudoconvex Stein tubular neighbourhoods.
item.dc:creator: Marko Slapar, Sa\v{s}o Strle

item.title: Quantitative hyperconvexity and the Bergman distance
item.description: arXiv:2610.34339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ be a bounded hyperconvex domain admitting a negative plurisubharmonic exhaustion function $u$ such that $-u(z)\le C\exp[-\eta(\log(1/\delta_\Omega(z)))]$ near the boundary, where $\eta$ is nondecreasing with $\lim_{t\rightarrow+\infty}\eta(t)=+\infty$. We present a lower bound for the Bergman distance $d_{B,\Omega}(z_0,z)$ by counting the iterates of a function determined by the generalized inverse of $\eta$. The bound tends to infinity as $z\rightarrow\partial\Omega$ for every such $\eta$; moreover, it recovers several known estimates. The proof combines a one-sided localization of Green sublevel sets with boundary estimates for the Bergman kernel and a capacity--volume inequality. We also obtain an upper bound for the Bergman distance along the axis of a family of complete Hartogs domains whose fiber radii decay faster than every positive power of the boundary distance in the base disc.
item.dc:creator: Bo-Yong Chen, Yuanpu Xiong

item.title: Lempert left inverses of the Royal and Flat geodesics of the symmetrized bidisc
item.description: arXiv:2610.34355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we give complete description of the Lempert left inverses of the royal and flat geodesics of the symmetrized bidisc. It is further proved that the collection of all such Lempert left inverses to the royal and flat geodesics is path connected. This, in particular, answers a question asked by Zwonek \cite[~Remark 4.4, 4.5]{zwonek}.
item.dc:creator: Naveen Gupta

item.title: Holomorphic Tischler fibration theorem for Stein spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.34383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a holomorphic analogue of Tischler approximation for closed differential forms normalized by a prescribed holomorphic vector field. The main setting consists of connected normal Stein spaces satisfying a degree-one reflexive Poincar\'e property, with finitely generated first integral homology and a holomorphic $\mathbb C^*$-action admitting a closed normalized reflexive one-form. Under these hypotheses, the given form can be approximated on compact subsets of the regular locus by closed normalized reflexive forms with discrete period groups. When the first Betti number is at least two, the approximating forms may be chosen with rank-two lattice periods. We relate these approximations to holomorphic locally trivial fibrations over quotients of $\mathbb C$, with connected Stein analytic fibers that may be singular. We also establish a finite-equivariant version for suitable Stein quotients and discuss the associated normalization obstructions, including those arising from local singularity topology. Further results concern closed holomorphic time forms, transverse foliations, and the relation between the period groups and the dynamics of complete holomorphic flows. Examples illustrate both the applicability and the limitations of the hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Scardua

item.title: A Levi-form criterion for Oka complements
item.description: arXiv:2610.34426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a connected Stein manifold of complex dimension at least three with the density property, then $M\setminus K$ is a connected Oka manifold for every nonempty compact $K\Subset M$ with smooth boundary whose Levi form has at least two nonnegative eigenvalues at every boundary point for local defining functions negative on $\operatorname{int}K$. For compact sets in $\mathbb{C}^n$ with smooth boundary, this settles both implications between pseudoconvexity of $\partial K$ and the Oka property of $\mathbb{C}^n\setminus K$: pseudoconvexity is sufficient but not necessary for $n\geq3$, and necessary but not sufficient for $n=2$. In dimension two, we give an explicit compact set in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with strongly pseudoconvex boundary and non-Oka complement.
item.dc:creator: Yun-Heng Du

item.title: Bounds for the univalent Bloch-Landau constant
item.description: arXiv:2610.34580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The univalent Bloch-Landau constant $\mathcal{U}$ is the largest number such that, for every univalent function $f$ on the unit disk, $f(\mathbb{D})$ contains a disk of radius $\mathcal{U} |f'(0)|$. We prove $0.612242\le\mathcal{U}<0.6562681$. The previous lower bound, $0.57088586$, came from growth estimates, which control disks centered at $f(0)$. Our improvement rests on a different mechanism. After Landau's normalization, a $2\times2$ compression of the Grunsky matrix constrains every omitted value through the same two coefficients, and choosing the center of the disk from these coefficients exploits this shared information. A short analytic proof based on this idea gives $\mathcal{U}\ge0.592$; it has been formalized in Lean, with the classical Grunsky and Fekete-Szeg\H{o} inequalities as the only external inputs. Retaining complex quadratic forms of the matrix gives $\mathcal{U}\ge0.612242$ through a finite interval certificate, and this bound holds for every normalized univalent function with $a_2=0$ and $|a_3|\le1/3$. We also show that no argument based on disks centered at $f(0)$ can give a bound above $0.6$. For the upper bound we construct an explicit domain, bounded by Goodman's first two slit generations, thirty analytic arcs and a circle. We certify $\mathcal{U}<0.6562681$ with a capacity estimate for almost critical arcs, improving the best published bound $0.6563937$.
item.dc:creator: Frank Wikstr\"om

item.title: Modular Existential Closedness
item.description: arXiv:2610.35409v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_n, j(\tau_1), \ldots, j(\tau_n)) \in V$ with $\tau_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouch\'e's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.
item.dc:creator: Vahagn Aslanyan

item.title: Movable Curves and Ample Normal Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.33724v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the movable cone of a smooth complex projective variety is the closed cone generated by possibly singular curves with ample coherent normal sheaves, answering a question of Boucksom--Demailly--P\u{a}un--Peternell. For smooth curves, we establish the analogous equality in several geometric settings and give explicit constructions on blowups.
item.dc:creator: Jingcao Wu

item.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.33890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is the second in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. We focus here on the geometrical origins of these groups, as first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265. The spaces we are interested in are spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi i (k-1)}{k}}\}$. We show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. Moreover, we show that the $k$-shuffle braid groups $\mathcal{B}_n(k)$ inject into the larger braid groups $\mathcal{B}_{nk}$.
item.dc:creator: Chlo\'e Postel-Vinay

item.title: Quasicircularity of the Zakeri Curve and Capture Component Boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.34225v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a fixed irrational rotation number of bounded type, we prove that the locus of critically marked cubic polynomials whose two critical points lie on the boundary of the fixed Siegel disk is a quasicircle. This locus is known as the Zakeri curve. The main step is a boundary correspondence lemma for holomorphic families of disks with uniformly quasiconformal extensions. We further prove that every capture component in this family is a quasidisk, including components attached to the Zakeri curve.
item.dc:creator: Yuming Fu, Weiwei Su

item.title: Gaussian zero-count fluctuations in annuli
item.description: arXiv:2610.34229v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine joint zero-count fluctuations of the self-dual weighted Szeg\H{o} Gaussian analytic function in fixed and thinning annuli. For a fixed annulus, the counts near its two boundary components converge jointly to independent standard normal variables after centering and marginal normalization, at arbitrary relative rates of boundary approach. This answers the simultaneous central limit question of Katori and Shirai for this model. The unscaled covariance converges to a negative constant, which we evaluate in complete elliptic integrals. A sharp variance asymptotic for the difference between an annular winding number and its coupled disk count yields quantitative normal approximation bounds. For thinning annuli with inner radius $q=e^{-h}$, the counts in every fixed finite family of interior transverse bands converge jointly to a Gaussian vector after centering and multiplication by $\sqrt h$. We give its spectral covariance matrix, prove strict negative covariance for disjoint bands, and identify its nullspace from the interval indicators. The fixed-annulus proof couples the Laurent series to two independent Gaussian power series. For thinning annuli, we combine exact periodization of a strip kernel, a uniform Laguerre-chaos tail bound, and connected Gaussian diagrams.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolin Zhu, Feng Guo

item.title: Positivity of Relative Pluricanonical Direct Images via Fixed-Point Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.35590v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a direct analytic approach to positivity of relative pluricanonical direct images through a fixed-point Hermitian metric by direct differential curvature calculations. The curvature resolvent formula from fixed-point equation leads to two-sided estimates of entire Nakano curvature by determinant curvature. In this way, we identify generic rank of determinant curvature with birational variation dimension for a projective algebraic fibration between smooth connected projective varieties with general fiber of general type and maximal birational variation, assuming $mK_F$ is globally generated or the $m$-canonical map is birational for general fiber $F$. In the global generation case, Green--Griffiths Conjecture asks for the tautological bigness of the ordinary symmetric powers $\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}f_*\omega_{X/Y}^{\otimes m}$, without passing to reflexive hulls, for $\ell\geq P_m(F)=h^0(F,mK_F)$ whenever $m\geq 1$. We prove it for all $\ell\geq1$ at levels $m\geq 2$, also in the case of birational $m$-canonical map, but construct a counterexample at level $m=1$. Over curves, curvature and boundary estimates give a direct analytic proof of Viehweg's ampleness theorem requested by Fujino. For smooth projective families, we also establish numerical dimension and vanishing results related to the birational variation dimension.
item.dc:creator: Jixiang Fu, Yunyang Xiao

item.title: On the topological invariance of the algebraic multiplicity of holomorphic foliations
item.description: arXiv:2407.09306v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we address one of the most basic and fundamental problems in the theory of foliations and ODEs, the topological invariance of the algebraic multiplicity of a holomorphic foliation. For instance, we prove an adapted version of A'Campo-L\^e's Theorem for foliations, i.e., the algebraic multiplicity equal to one is a topological invariant in dimension two. This result is further generalized to higher dimensions under mild conditions; as a consequence, we prove that saddle-nodes are topologically invariant. We prove that the algebraic multiplicity is a topological invariant in several classes of foliations that contain, for instance, the generalized curves and the foliations of second type. Additionally, we address a fundamental result by Rosas-Bazan, which states that the existence of a homeomorphism extending through a neighborhood of the exceptional divisor of the first blow-up implies the topological invariance of the algebraic multiplicity. We show that the result holds if the homeomorphism extends locally near a singularity, even if it does not extend over the entire divisor.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo M. C\^amara, Fernando Reis, Jos\'e Edson Sampaio

item.title: Modulus estimates and cavitation in higher dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2512.18731v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explore the phenomenon of cavitation in higher-dimensional elasticity, defining it as the mapping of a punctured ball onto a non-degenerate ring domain. Crucially, for the class of locally quasiconformal mappings (or more general mappings) defined on the punctured ball $0<|x|<1$ in $\mathbb R^n$ that we examine, cavitation is equivalent to a failure of continuous extension to the origin. While existing modulus estimates prove insufficient for reliably detecting cavitation in this setting, our study establishes refined modulus bounds. This is achieved by introducing a novel directional dilatation which, in conjunction with the known angular dilatation, overcomes the limitations of previous methods. We illustrate our theoretical findings with several examples that demonstrate both cavitation occurrence and its absence.
item.dc:creator: Anatoly Golberg, Vladimir Gutlyanski\u{i}, Vladimir Ryazanov, Toshiyuki Sugawa

item.title: Fractional Besov-Sobolev Spaces on Chord-arc Curves
item.description: arXiv:2601.01348v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a bounded rectifiable Jordan curve, with complementary domains $\Omega_i$ and $\Omega_e$. For $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$, we study the spaces $\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(\Omega)$ of harmonic functions satisfying \[ \iint_\Omega |\nabla u(z)|^p \operatorname{dist}(z,\Gamma)^{(1-s)p-1}\,dA(z)<\infty, \qquad \Omega\in\{\Omega_i,\Omega_e\}. \] When $\Gamma$ is the unit circle, the traces of these two spaces coincide with the fractional Besov-Sobolev space $B^s_{p,p}(\Gamma)$. The equivalence of boundary seminorms and harmonic energies on the circle raises a geometric question: which rough curves preserve these estimates? For every radial-Lipschitz curve $\Gamma$, we prove \[ \operatorname{Tr}_\Gamma\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(\Omega_i) =B_{p,p}^s(\Gamma) =\operatorname{Tr}_\Gamma\mathcal B_{p,p}^s(\Omega_e) \] whenever either $1 < p < 2$ and $2/p - 1 \leq s < 1$, $2 < p < \infty$ and $0 < s \leq 1/2 + 1/p$ or $p=2$ and $0<s<1$. For arbitrary chord-arc curves, the same trace identities hold when $1/p\le s<1/2+1/(2p)$. Taking $s=1-1/p$ yields an almost-Dirichlet principle for the unweighted $p$-energy on radial-Lipschitz domains when $3/2\le p\le4$. Here, the upper bound $4$ is sharp. In particular, every Riemann map $g:\Omega_i\to\mathbb D_i$ from a bounded radial-Lipschitz domain satisfies $g'\in L^4(\Omega_i)$, and the exponent $4$ is optimal uniformly over this class. This gives a sharp endpoint counterpart of Brennan's integrability conclusion for radial-Lipschitz domains.
item.dc:creator: Huaying Wei, Michel Zinsmeister

item.title: Recurrence Relations for the Maclaurin Coefficients of Products of Elementary Functions and the Bessel Functions
item.description: arXiv:2601.18332v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate recurrence relations for the Maclaurin coefficients of the products of a elementary function and the Bessel function of the first kind $\mathcal{J}(z) = h(z) J_\nu(z)$ and the modified Bessel function of the first kind $\mathcal{I}(z) = h(z) I_\nu(z)$ in the complex plane corresponding to several specific choices of $h(z)$. In particular, we specialize $h(z)$ as $e^{pz}$, $(1-\theta z)^p$, $e^{-p \arctan z}$, $\sin(pz)$, $\cos(pz)$, $\sinh(pz)$, $\cosh(pz)$, $\arcsin(pz)$ and $\arccos(pz)$.
item.dc:creator: Zhong-Xuan Mao, Jing-Feng Tian

item.title: Geometry of bounded domains with piecewise smooth boundary
item.description: arXiv:2604.27337v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the geometry of bounded domains with piecewise smooth boundary. Specifically, we obtain the relationship between the squeezing function corresponding to polydisk and Levi flatness on bounded convex domains. As an application, we prove that a two-dimensional bounded generic convex domain with piecewise $C^2$-smooth boundary that is not smooth and admits a finite volume quotient is biholomorphic to bidisk. Moreover, we show that any Teichm\"uller space $\mathcal{T}_g$ with $g\geq2$ cannot be biholomorphic to a bounded domain with piecewise $C^2$-smooth boundary.
item.dc:creator: Xingsi Pu, Lang Wang

item.title: The $p$--Bloch--Carleson measure problem for $0<p<\infty$: A complete characterization via Carleson tents
item.description: arXiv:2606.16760v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize the boundedness and compactness of the embedding $$ \operatorname{id}:\mathcal B \longrightarrow L^p(\mu),\qquad 0<p<\infty, $$ where $\mathcal B$ denotes the Bloch space and $\mu$ is a positive Borel measure on the unit disc. The criteria depend only on the dyadic Carleson tents. These results refine our earlier $L^2(\mu)$ characterization based on a full dyadic resolution of the disc and extend it to all positive exponents. The proof combines discretization on Carleson tents, representations of Bloch functions by series of analytic polynomials, and weighted matrix estimates. We also obtain corresponding boundedness and compactness characterizations for $$ \textrm{id}:\mathcal Q_p\longrightarrow L^q(\mu),\qquad 0<p\le1,\quad 0<q<\infty. $$ These results resolve the general $p$--Bloch--Carleson measure problem studied by Girela, Pel\'aez, P\'erez-Gonz\'alez and R\"atty\"a in 2008.
item.dc:creator: Bingyang Hu, Xiaojing Zhou

item.title: A Counterexample to the Holomorphic Cancellation Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.12581v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that if a contractible Stein manifold $X$ with the density property admits a proper holomorphic embedding into $\mathbb{C}^k$, then $X \times \mathbb{C}^k$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^{n+k}$ with $n=\dim X$. We also prove that McLean's exotic affine variety $K_n$, $n\ge4$, a smooth contractible affine variety which is not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^n$, has the density property. Hence for $n \ge 4$ there exist an integer $m \in \{ n, \dots, 2n\}$ and an affine variety $X$ such that $X \times \mathbb{C}$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^{m+1}$ and $X$ is not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^m$. This settles the Holomorphic Cancellation Problem in the negative. We also construct holomorphic actions of $\mathbb{C}^*$ and finite cyclic groups on complex Euclidean spaces that are not topologically conjugate to linear actions.
item.dc:creator: Gaofeng Huang

item.title: Kobayashi completeness of pseudoconvex domains: finite type and a smooth counterexample
item.description: arXiv:2610.28833v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb C^N$ with $C^\infty$ boundary of finite D'Angelo one-type is Kobayashi complete. As a separate consequence of our criterion of completeness and an estimate of Diederich--Forn\ae ss, we prove that every bounded pseudoconvex domain with real-analytic boundary is Kobayashi complete. We then show that smoothness alone does not imply completeness: there exists a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb C^3$ with $C^\infty$ boundary and a global smooth plurisubharmonic defining function whose Kobayashi and Carath\'eodory distances are incomplete.
item.dc:creator: Armen Edigarian

item.title: A Complex Geometric Approach to the Discrete Gabor Transform and Localization Operators on the Flat Torus
item.description: arXiv:2410.15170v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In a recent paper, the discrete Gabor transform was connected to a Gabor transform with a time frequency domain given by the flat torus. We show that the corresponding Bargmann-Fock spaces can be expressed as theta functions (or equivalently line bundles on Abelian varieties). We give applications of this viewpoint to frame results for the discrete Gabor transform. In particular, we get necessary conditions which hold in higher dimensions and can expand the known results in the one dimensional case, the primary tool being the theorem of the square. We also give an application to asymptotics of restriction operators which arises via the asymptotic behavior of Bergman kernels and Toeplitz operators for high tensor powers of line bundles and find that discrete time frequency restriction operators will exhibit "plunge" behaviors similar to those of time frequency restriction operators in other contexts.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Testorf

item.title: Explicit complex time integrators for stiff problems
item.description: arXiv:2601.07730v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Most numerical methods for time integration use real-valued time steps. Complex time steps, however, can provide an additional degree of freedom, as we can select the magnitude of the time step in both the real and imaginary directions. We show that specific paths in the complex time plane lead to expanded stability regions, providing clear computational advantages for complex-valued systems. In particular, we highlight the Schr\"odinger equation, for which complex time integrators can be uniquely optimal. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these benefits extend to certain classes of real-valued stiff systems by coupling complex time steps with the Projective Integration method.
item.dc:creator: Jithin D. George, Julian Koellermeier, Samuel Y. Jung, Niall M. Mangan

item.title: Comparing positive Toeplitz operators on holomorphic and pluriharmonic Fock spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.13550v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove sharp norm comparisons between positive Toeplitz operators associated with the same positive Borel measure, acting respectively on holomorphic functions and on sums of holomorphic and antiholomorphic functions, both equipped with the Gaussian-weighted $L^2$ norm. For every positive Borel measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $0<p<\infty$, both operators are compact with summable $p$th powers of their singular values (i.e. Schatten) exactly when $z\mapsto\mu(B(z,r))$ belongs to $L^p(\mathbb{C}^n)$ for some fixed radius $r>0$. For other weights, this agreement can fail dramatically. We construct a weight $e^{-2\phi}$ and a finite positive measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{C}$ for which the operator on holomorphic functions has the same singular values as with the Gaussian weight and the same measure $\mu$. These values have summable $p$th powers for every $p>0$, yet the quadratic form on sums of holomorphic and antiholomorphic functions is unbounded in weighted $L^2$. The example still satisfies $\Delta\phi=2$, as for the Gaussian choice $\phi(z)=|z|^2/2$.
item.dc:creator: Sam Looi

item.title: Surjectivity of real-linear Cauchy--Riemann operators: from the minimal Harder--Narasimhan slope to automatic transversality
item.description: arXiv:2608.18997v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper relates the minimal Harder--Narasimhan slope to the surjectivity of real-linear Cauchy--Riemann operators. We establish a conformally invariant $L^2$ criterion and an asymptotic slope criterion, which yield higher-rank automatic transversality criteria for pseudoholomorphic curves beyond the classical rank-one framework. Applications to pseudoholomorphic spheres in $S^6$ provide quantitative $L^2$ obstructions to the integrability of almost complex structures.
item.dc:creator: Qingchun Ji, Jun Yao

item.title: Failure of the local decay formula for Arnold multiplicities under twisted K\"ahler--Ricci flow
item.description: arXiv:2608.30302v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Di Nezza--Guedj--Lu asked whether local Arnold multiplicities under maximal weak twisted K\"ahler--Ricci flow with fixed cohomology class satisfy $\lambda(\varphi_t,x)=\max\{\lambda(\varphi_0,x)-t,0\}$. We construct counterexamples with analytic initial singularities in every dimension $n\ge2$. On the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e$, $e\ge2$, the initial current $[S]+(e+1)[F]$ yields $\lambda(\varphi_t,x)=1/2-t/e$ for $x\in S\setminus F$ and $0<t<e/2$, where $S$ is the negative section and $F$ a fibre. Products with smooth stationary factors give higher-dimensional examples. The Zariski negative part of $\{S\}+\{F\}$, the reduced support class, forces extra divisor mass. For pure divisorial data with simple normal crossings support, a smooth semipositive representative of the reduced support class's positive part gives exact short-time formulas. On one surface we construct flows with identical initial current germs, background data and global initial Arnold multiplicity, but different local rates.

item.title: Measures of maximal entropy for meromorphic maps on compact K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.28617v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $f$ be a dominant meromorphic self-map of a compact K\"ahler manifold. Assume that $f$ has a strictly dominant intermediate dynamical degree $\lambda$ and that the number of isolated $n$-periodic points, counted with multiplicity, is at most $\lambda^n+o(\lambda^n)$. Then $f$ admits at most one adapted invariant probability measure of entropy $\log\lambda$. If such a measure exists, its natural extension is Bernoulli, and the isolated periodic points equidistribute towards it when counted with or without multiplicity. We apply this criterion to several classes of maps in complex dynamics, resolving longstanding open problems.
item.dc:creator: Muhan Luo, Qi Zhou
